implemented: GET /v1/catalog parses complete decimal bbox fields, enforces CRS84 bounds and a maximum one-degree span per axis, and limits results to 1000 supported approaches. Intersections without supported approaches are not advertised.

HTTP and WebSocket share one snapshot gate requiring matching current catalog version, active enabled straight approach, complete provider identity, verified generation time and known units. Null timing, expired phase/TTL, future or old source times and unknown signals are unavailable. Verified flashing state is displayed as flashing, never a green arrival prediction.
Transport safety uses a maximum source/receipt age of 5000ms; this conservative cutoff does not establish provider units or source-time semantics.
WebSocket registration is awaited before upgrade route declaration. Malformed JSON is handled as a protocol error rather than escaping the message callback.
Subscribe sends complete current state, never a delta requiring a prior connection. Messages carry requestId, streamEpoch and per-connection sequence.
A shared 250ms poll reads the current PostgreSQL catalog and emits changed snapshots, expiry and catalog invalidations. Database read failures produce unavailable; query time is bounded.

Bounds: 2048-byte incoming payload, 128-character requestId, 512-character approach/version keys, 32 subscriptions per connection, 64 connections, 20 messages per second per connection, and 65536-byte outgoing buffer. Heartbeats terminate unresponsive peers; shutdown removes timers and connections.
GET /v1/time returns no-store server receipt/send UTC milliseconds. Mobile bounds clock uncertainty using measured round-trip time instead of assuming matching clocks.
The separate loopback replay executable drives real HTTP/time/WebSocket routes with explicitly synthetic observations. Production startup never imports it, and it refuses NODE_ENV=production.
